lane: Qwen3.8-27B INT4 headline (R256 image, TP2, XPU graphs FULL_DECODE_ONLY 1-8, draft-only INT4 head, MTP depth 4, strict launcher env)
method: vLLM torch profiler over one 64-token greedy completion (22-token prompt) after two warm-ups; traces per rank; python_function tracing inflates wall time (62 tok/s inside the window vs 112 unprofiled), so only the relative split is used

device_kernels_rank0.note: rank 0 spends 280 ms inside the ring all-reduce kernel where rank 1 spends 3.5 ms: rank 0 waits for rank 1 at every eager all-reduce (the drafter runs eagerly; the verify step is a captured graph whose kernels the XPU profiler does not itemize)

reading: The step is host-bound. Within execute_model the eager draft passes (propose) are about half of the CPU time; the verify graph's replay costs little CPU; between steps the worker idles on the scheduler round trip. 716 int4 GEMM launches for 22 decode steps (about 40 per step from the 4 draft passes) plus 405 all-reduce calls. Capturing the draft loop (V2 model runner, R263) or cutting the per-step host path is the lever; larger decode graphs (R261) are not.

R264b_c2_c8_profile_no_stack.c2: window 2.8 s: 1.05 s of Dynamo recompilation (3 frames) on the first two-sequence batch = the single-pass ladder c2 stall; not recurring at c4/c8
R264b_c2_c8_profile_no_stack.c8: window 1735 ms, 20 uniform steps of 8x5 tokens: device kernels 381 ms (gemm 290, GDN chunk kernels ~25), CPU dominated by aten::index/copy_/to in the eager draft passes and sampling; cards busy ~25% of the time; 300 tok/s under the profiler (398 unprofiled)

R274_c32_profile_no_stack.window: 6.6 s: 1.08 s Dynamo recompilation on the first 32-sequence batch, 1.0 s mixed prefill step (583 prompt tokens), 20 uniform decode steps of 32x5=160 tokens in 3.24 s (162 ms/step)
R274_c32_profile_no_stack.reading: At c32 the cards are ~74% busy: the step is device-bound, not host-bound. Two components explain the c16->c32 collapse: (1) the GDN speculative path switches from the chunked kernels seen at c8 (~1 ms/step) to gdn::gated_delta_rule_spec_kernel at 27 ms/step; (2) the W4A16 verify GEMMs scale ~linearly above M~32 (dequant-bound), 58 ms at M=160. The verify runs eagerly (160 tokens > captured sizes), costing ~24 ms of launch CPU per step that larger capture sizes would remove (R275).

R274b_c32_profile_group64.config: R274 with VLLM_XPU_GDN_SPEC_GROUP=64 (ungrouped GDN spec branch at 32 sequences)
R274b_c32_profile_group64.reading: Without grouping the c32 step is device-bound (96 of 108 ms): W4A16 GEMM 55 ms at M=160 and the GDN speculative recurrent kernel 27 ms (48 layers x 0.56 ms for 32 sequences; grouped 2x16 cost the same 27 ms, so the kernel's time is linear in sequences: ~17.6 us per sequence per layer, no cross-sequence parallelism). The grouped path (R274) added ~40 ms of host work per step (sync + gather/scatter per layer). Graph capture above 16 sequences fails on the grouped branch's .tolist() (R275); R276 makes the boundaries arithmetic.

R274c_c16_profile_group16.config: R274 script at c16 (80-token verify inside a captured graph, capture sizes to 80)
R274c_c16_profile_group16.note: the captured verify's kernels are not itemized by the XPU profiler; the visible 13.5 ms are the eager draft passes (29 gemm launches, 1 all-gather per pass) and the CPU side is one blocking copy waiting on the graph. 16 x ~2.7 tokens per 65 ms step is ~650 tok/s of steady aggregate, in line with the warm ladder's 580 once prefill and ramp are included.

R278j2.config: launcher chain, group 64, capture sizes to 320
R278j2.note: verify inside a captured graph (not itemized); plain-client batches 337-368 tok/s

R278k.config: launcher chain, group 64, capture sizes 1-8 (eager verify)

R278j2_R278k_launcher_chain_c32_profiles.root_cause: VLLM_XPU_W4A16_DETERMINISM_PAD absent from every runner-launched container (the launcher chain did not forward it); the R213b overlay defaults to ON and pads 128-512 rows to 512 before the W4A16 GEMM: 3x GEMM work at M=160 (529 vs 180 us per launch), no effect below 128 rows (c1-c16). Direct docker-run scripts passed the variable as 0. GPU clocks 2.4-2.8 GHz on both cards throughout (not frequency). Fix: both launchers now forward the pad switches with 0 as the default; R281 re-measures the published ladders.
